# OuroProvider

Optional app-level provider that routes internal `href`s through your router's link. Ouro UI components work without it: they honor reduced motion themselves, in CSS (`motion-reduce:` variants and `prefers-reduced-motion` queries), and need no animation library. If your app animates with Motion, wrap it in `<MotionConfig reducedMotion="user">` for the same behavior.

```tsx
import { OuroProvider } from "@/registry/ouro/lib/ouro/ouro-provider";
```

## Example

```tsx
const RouterLink = (props: ComponentProps<OuroLinkComponent>) => <Link to={props.href} {...props} />;
<OuroProvider linkComponent={RouterLink}><App /></OuroProvider>
```

## Usage

Type a custom adapter with `ComponentProps<OuroLinkComponent>` so it always compiles, including under `exactOptionalPropertyTypes`.

In Next.js, render it from a client file, such as `app/providers.tsx` starting with `"use client"`, that passes `next/link`'s `Link` (`<OuroProvider linkComponent={Link}>`), and wrap the app in it from `app/layout.tsx`: a Server Component can't pass `Link`, a function, to a client component. The README's "Next.js" section has both files.

## Props

Type: `OuroProviderProps`.

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `children` (required) | `ReactNode` |  | Your app, or the part of it that uses Ouro UI. |
| `linkComponent` | `OuroLinkComponent` |  | Renders internal `href`s, for example an adapter around a router's `Link`. |

## Types

### `OuroLinkComponent`

A component that renders an internal link, such as a router's `Link`.

```ts
type OuroLinkComponent = ComponentType<
  AnchorHTMLAttributes<HTMLAnchorElement> & { href: string; ref?: Ref<HTMLAnchorElement> }
>;
```
